!.description: Execute {cmd} in the shell and show its output; with [range], filter those lines through {cmd}.

&.description: Repeat the last :substitute in [range] lines. :& uses the same search pattern, :~ uses the last used search pattern. [&] keeps the flags.

<.description: Shift [range] lines one 'shiftwidth' left. Repeat the < to shift several times, e.g. :<<<.

=.description: Show the line number of the last line of [range] (default: the last line in the file). With the l, # or p flag, also show the line text.

>.description: Shift [range] lines one 'shiftwidth' right. Repeat the > to shift several times, e.g. :>>>.

@.description: Execute the contents of {register} as an Ex command at [line]. :@: repeats the last command line and :@@ repeats the previous :@.

IdeaPlug.description: Enable the IdeaVim extension with the quoted {name}, similar to Plug in vim-plug.

N[ext].description: Go to the [count]th previous editor tab, wrapping around at the first one.

P[rint].description: Show [range] lines (default current line) in the output panel, prefixed with line numbers if 'number' is set.

Plug[in].description: Enable the IdeaVim extension named in quotes, using vim-plug syntax, e.g. Plug 'tpope/vim-surround'.

a[ppend].description: Insert the lines typed after this command below [line].

ab[breviate].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

abc[lear].description: Remove all abbreviations for the mode of the command: Insert and Command-line, Insert only, or Command-line only. Use <buffer> for buffer-local ones.

abo[veleft].description: Make the following command put its new window above or left of the current one.

action.description: Execute the IDE action with the given {action-id}.

ar[gs].description: List the argument list, with the current file in square brackets.

arga[dd].description: Add the files to the argument list after the current one.

argd[elete].description: Delete the files matching {pattern} from the argument list.

argdo.description: Run {cmd} for every file in the argument list.

arge[dit].description: Add {name} to the argument list and edit it.

argg[lobal].description: Define the global argument list, which every window shares.

argl[ocal].description: Define a local argument list for this window.

argu[ment].description: Go to the [count]th editor tab in the current window.

as[cii].description: Print the decimal, hexadecimal and octal value of the character under the cursor.

au[tocmd].description: Register {cmd} to run when one of the comma-separated {event}s fires for a file matching {pat}. With [!], remove all registered autocommands.

aug[roup].description: Start the autocommand group {name} for the following :autocmd commands; END returns to the default group. With [!], clear group {name}.

b[uffer].description: Edit buffer [N], alternate buffer #, or the open file matching {name}; [!] ignores unsaved changes.

ba[ll].description: Open a window for each buffer in the argument list.

bad[d].description: Add the files to the argument list after the current one.

bd[elete].description: Close the buffer, or the buffers in [range].

be[have].description: Set 'selectmode', 'mousemodel', 'keymodel' and 'selection' for mswin or xterm behaviour.

bel[owright].description: Make the following command put its new window below or right of the current one.

bf[irst].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

bl[ast].description: Go to the last file, buffer or tab.

bm[odified].description: Go to the [count] next buffer with unwritten changes.

bn[ext].description: Go to the [count]th next editor tab.

bo[tright].description: Make the following command put its new window at the very bottom or far right.

bp[revious].description: Go to the [count]th previous editor tab, wrapping around at the first one.

br[ewind].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

breaka[dd].description: Add a Vimscript breakpoint. Accepted and does nothing: there is no debugger.

buffers.description: List all open buffers, optionally filtered by the flags +, =, a, % and #.

bun[load].description: Close the buffer, or the buffers in [range].

bw[ipeout].description: Close the buffer, or the buffers in [range].

cN[ext].description: Go to the [count] previous error in the quickfix list.

c[hange].description: Replace the lines in [range] with the lines typed after this command.

ca[bbrev].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

cabc[lear].description: Remove all abbreviations for the mode of the command: Insert and Command-line, Insert only, or Command-line only. Use <buffer> for buffer-local ones.

cadde[xpr].description: Read errors from {expr} and add them to the quickfix list without jumping.

cal[l].description: Call the function {name} with the given arguments and discard the result, optionally for a [range] of lines.

cb[uffer].description: Read the lines of a buffer into the quickfix list.

cc.description: Go to error [nr] in the quickfix list, or the current one again.

cd.description: Change the working directory to [path], or to the home directory with no argument.

ce[nter].description: Centre the lines in [range] within [width] columns, 'textwidth' by default.

cex[pr].description: Read errors from {expr} into the quickfix list and jump to the first.

cf[ile].description: Read the error file into the quickfix list and jump to the first error.

cfir[st].description: Go to error [count] in the quickfix list, the first by default.

changes.description: List the change list, the places where the text was last changed.

chd[ir].description: Change the working directory to [path], or to the home directory with no argument.

checkt[ime].description: Check whether a file has changed on disk. Accepted and does nothing: VS Code watches the file itself.

cla[st].description: Go to error [count] from the end of the quickfix list, the last by default.

cle[arjumps].description: Clear the jump list of the current window.

clo[se].description: Close the current editor. :close and :hide behave the same way as :quit in IdeaVim.

cm[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

cmapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

cn[ext].description: Go to the [count] next error in the quickfix list.

cno[remap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

cnorea[bbrev].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

co[py].description: Copy the lines in [range] to below line {address}.

colo[rscheme].description: Load a colour scheme. Accepted and does nothing: the theme is VS Code's.

com[mand].description: Define the user command {cmd} that executes {rep}. Without arguments, list all user-defined commands.

comp[iler].description: Set the compiler plugin. Accepted and does nothing: there are no compiler plugins.

conf[irm].description: Run {cmd} and ask rather than fail when it would lose a change.

cp[revious].description: Go to the [count] previous error in the quickfix list.

cq[uit].description: Quit with an error code. Accepted and does nothing: there is no exit code to give.

crewind.description: Go to error [count] in the quickfix list, the first by default.

cu[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

cuna[bbrev].description: Remove abbreviation {lhs} for the mode of the command. Use <buffer> to remove a buffer-local abbreviation.

d[elete].description: Delete the lines in [range] (default current line) into register [x]. A [count] deletes [count] lines starting with the last line in [range].

delf[unction].description: Delete the user-defined function {name}. With [!], do not report an error if the function does not exist.

delm[arks].description: Delete the specified {marks}; ranges like a-d are allowed. With [!], delete all lowercase marks of the current file.

diffg[et].description: Take a change from the other side of the diff. Accepted and does nothing: the diff is VS Code's.

diffo[ff].description: Leave diff mode in this window, or with [!] in every window of this tab.

diffp[atch].description: Apply the patch in {patchfile} to the current buffer and diff the result.

diffpu[t].description: Put a change to the other side of the diff. Accepted and does nothing, as :diffget is.

diffs[plit].description: Split the window and diff it against {file}.

difft[his].description: Make this window part of the diff.

dig[raphs].description: Without arguments, list the available digraphs; with [!], also show headers. With {char1}{char2} {number} pairs, define new digraphs.

dis[play].description: Display the type and contents of all registers, or only of the registers named in {arg}.

do[autocmd].description: Run the autocommands for {event} as if it had just happened, in the current buffer.

doautoa[ll].description: Run the autocommands for {event} as if it had just happened, in every loaded buffer.

ea[rlier].description: Go to an older state of the text: [count] changes back, or {N}s, {N}m, {N}h back in time, or {N}f file writes back.

ec[ho].description: Evaluate each {expr} and display the results separated by spaces.

echoe[rr].description: Echo the expressions as an error message and keep it in the message history.

echoh[l].description: Use the highlight group {name} for the echo commands that follow.

echom[sg].description: Echo the expressions and keep the result in the message history.

echon.description: Echo the expressions with no line break after them.

ene[w].description: Open a new, empty buffer in the current window.

ev[al].description: Evaluate {expr} and throw the result away, for an expression called for its effect.

exe[cute].description: Evaluate each {expr} and execute the resulting string as an Ex command. Multiple arguments are joined with a space.

exi[t].description: Save the current file and close its editor.

exu[sage].description: Show Ex command help. Accepted and does nothing: :help lists the commands instead.

f[ile].description: Display the current file name, cursor position and file status.

files.description: List all open buffers, optionally filtered by the flags +, =, a, % and #.

filet[ype].description: Switch filetype detection on or off. Accepted and does nothing: VS Code detects the language itself.

filt[er].description: Run {cmd} and show only the output lines matching /{pattern}/, or not matching it with [!].

fin[d].description: Find {file} in the project and open it. Without an argument, open the IDE's Go to File popup.

fir[st].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

foldc[lose].description: Close the folds in [range]. With [!] close them all the way up.

foldd[oopen].description: Run {cmd} on every line not in a closed fold.

folddoc[losed].description: Run {cmd} on every line in a closed fold.

foldo[pen].description: Open the folds in [range]. With [!] open them all the way down.

fu[nction].description: List all user-defined functions, the definition of the function {name}, or the functions matching /{pattern}.

g[lobal].description: Execute the Ex command [cmd] (default :p) on the lines in [range] (default whole file) that match {pattern}. With :g! or :v, use the lines that do not match.

go[to].description: Go to byte [count] in the file, default the first character.

gr[ep].description: Run 'grepprg', read its matches into the quickfix list and jump to the first.

gu[i].description: Start the GUI. Accepted and does nothing: this is already one.

gv[im].description: Start the GUI. Accepted and does nothing, as :gui is.

h[elp].description: Open Vimperor's help and jump to the subject, e.g. dd, v_d, i_CTRL-W or :s. Without a subject, show the start of the help.

ha[rdcopy].description: Print the buffer. Accepted and does nothing: printing is VS Code's.

helpg[rep].description: Search the help files. Accepted and does nothing: :help lists the commands instead.

helpt[ags].description: Generate help tags. Accepted and does nothing: the help is rendered rather than read from files.

hi[ghlight].description: Define or clear a highlight group, which is what :match and the extensions paint with.

hid[e].description: Close the current editor. :close and :hide behave the same way as :quit in IdeaVim.

his[tory].description: Display the history of the given {name} type (cmd, search, expr, input or all), default command-line history. An optional {first},{last} limits the entries shown.

hor[izontal].description: Make the following command split horizontally.

i[nsert].description: Insert the lines typed after this command above [line].

ia[bbrev].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

iabc[lear].description: Remove all abbreviations for the mode of the command: Insert and Command-line, Insert only, or Command-line only. Use <buffer> for buffer-local ones.

ij[ump].description: Jump to a match in the included files. Accepted and does nothing, as :isearch is.

il[ist].description: List the matches in the included files. Accepted and does nothing, as :isearch is.

im[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

imapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

ino[remap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

inorea[bbrev].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

int[ro].description: Show the intro screen. Accepted and does nothing.

is[earch].description: Search the included files. Accepted and does nothing: there is no include search.

isp[lit].description: Split and jump to a match in the included files. Accepted and does nothing, as :isearch is.

iu[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

iuna[bbrev].description: Remove abbreviation {lhs} for the mode of the command. Use <buffer> to remove a buffer-local abbreviation.

j[oin].description: Join the lines in [range], or [count] lines starting at the last line in [range]. With [!], do not insert or remove any spaces.

ju[mps].description: Print the jump list, marking the current position with >.

k.description: Set mark {a-zA-Z'} at the last line of [range] (default current line), column 0.

kee[pmarks].description: Run {cmd} keeping the marks where they are, for a filter command.

keepa[lt].description: Run {cmd} without changing the alternate file.

keepj[umps].description: Run {cmd} without changing the jump list or the change list.

keepp[atterns].description: Run {cmd} without changing the last search pattern.

lN[ext].description: Go to the [count] previous error in the location list.

l[ist].description: Print the lines in [range] with unprintable characters shown as in 'list' mode.

la[st].description: Go to the last file, buffer or tab.

ladde[xpr].description: Read errors from {expr} and add them to the location list without jumping.

lan[guage].description: Set the language used for messages, time or collation. Accepted and does nothing here.

lat[er].description: Go to a newer state of the text, undoing an :earlier. Takes the same counts and time arguments.

lb[uffer].description: Read the lines of a buffer into the location list of the current window.

lc[d].description: Change the working directory for this window or tab only.

lch[dir].description: Change the working directory for this window or tab only.

le[ft].description: Left-align the lines in [range], with an indent of [indent] spaces.

lefta[bove].description: Make the following command put its new window above or left of the current one.

let.description: Assign the value of {expr} to the variable, option or register {var}. Operators like += and .= are supported.

lex[pr].description: Read errors from {expr} into the location list of the current window.

lf[ile].description: Read the error file into the location list of the current window.

lfir[st].description: Go to error [count] in the location list, the first by default.

lgr[ep].description: Run 'grepprg' and read its matches into the location list of the current window.

ll.description: Go to error [nr] in the location list, or the current one again.

lla[st].description: Go to error [count] from the end of the location list, the last by default.

lli[st].description: Show the location list of the current window.

lm[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

lmak[e].description: Run 'makeprg' and read its errors into the location list of the current window.

lmapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

ln[oremap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

lne[xt].description: Go to the [count] next error in the location list.

loadk[eymap].description: In a sourced keymap file, start the list of {from} {to} key pairs used for language mappings (:lmap).

loadv[iew].description: Restore a view saved by :mkview. Accepted and does nothing, as :mkview is.

lockm[arks].description: Run {cmd} without the marks following the lines it changes.

lockv[ar].description: Lock the variable {name} so it can no longer be changed. A [depth] also locks nested List and Dictionary items.

lop[en].description: Show the location list of the current window.

lp[revious].description: Go to the [count] previous error in the location list.

lrewind.description: Go to error [count] in the location list, the first by default.

ls.description: List all open buffers, optionally filtered by the flags +, =, a, % and #.

lt[ag].description: Jump to the tag [name] and fill the location list with the matches.

lu[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

lua.description: Run Lua. Accepted and does nothing: there is no Lua interface.

lv[imgrep].description: Like :vimgrep, filling the location list of the current window.

lvimgrepa[dd].description: Like :lvimgrep, adding to the location list rather than replacing it.

lw[indow].description: Show the location list of the current window.

m[ove].description: Move the lines in [range] to below line {address}.

ma[rk].description: Set mark {a-zA-Z'} at the last line of [range] (default current line), column 0.

mak[e].description: Run 'makeprg', read its errors into the quickfix list and jump to the first.

map.description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

mapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

marks.description: List all marks, or only the marks named in {arg}.

mat[ch].description: Highlight everything matching /{pattern}/ with {group}, until :match none.

mes[sages].description: Show the message history. With [clear] empty it.

mk[exrc].description: Write the current mappings and settings to [file], like :mkvimrc with an ex name.

mks[ession].description: Write a session file. Accepted and does nothing: the layout is VS Code's.

mksp[ell].description: Compile a spell file. Accepted and does nothing, as :spelldump is.

mkv[imrc].description: Write the current mappings and settings to [file], ~/.vimperorrc by default.

mkvie[w].description: Save the view of the window to a file. Accepted and does nothing: the layout is VS Code's.

n[ext].description: Go to the [count]th next editor tab.

new.description: Split the window and open a new, empty buffer in it.

nm[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

nmapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

nn[oremap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

no[remap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

noh[lsearch].description: Stop highlighting matches of the last search pattern until the next search.

norea[bbrev].description: Define abbreviation {lhs} for {rhs} in Insert and/or Command-line mode; the norea forms are not remapped. Without {rhs}, list matching abbreviations.

norm[al].description: Execute {commands} as Normal mode keys, once for each line in [range]. With [!], mappings are not used.

noswapf[ile].description: Run {cmd} without a swap file for the buffers it opens.

nu[mber].description: Print the lines in [range] with their line numbers.

nun[map].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

o[pen].description: Start open mode. Accepted and does nothing: open mode is not implemented.

om[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

omapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

on[ly].description: Close all editor windows (splits) except the current one.

ono[remap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

opt[ions].description: Open the option window. Accepted and does nothing: use :set to see an option.

ou[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

ow[nsyntax].description: Give this window its own syntax. Accepted and does nothing: the language is VS Code's.

p[rint].description: Show [range] lines (default current line) in the output panel, prefixed with line numbers if 'number' is set.

pa[ckadd].description: Load the optional package {name}. Only matchit is supported, which enables the 'matchit' option.

packl[oadall].description: Load every package in 'packpath'. Accepted and does nothing: there is no package directory.

pc[lose].description: Close the preview window. Accepted and does nothing: there is no preview window.

pe[rl].description: Run Perl. Accepted and does nothing: there is no Perl interface.

ped[it].description: Edit a file in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing, as :pclose is.

po[p].description: Jump [count] entries back (older) in the tag stack, returning to where the tag jump was made.

prev[ious].description: Go to the [count]th previous editor tab, wrapping around at the first one.

prof[ile].description: Profile the Vimscript that runs, and write the report to {file}.

ps[earch].description: Show a match in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing, as :ptag is.

ptN[ext].description: Show the previous matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing.

pt[ag].description: Show a tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing: there is no preview window.

ptf[irst].description: Show the first matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing.

ptj[ump].description: Jump to a tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing, as :ptag is.

ptl[ast].description: Show the last matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing.

ptn[ext].description: Show the next matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing, as :ptag is.

ptp[revious].description: Show the previous matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing.

ptr[ewind].description: Show the first matching tag in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing.

pts[elect].description: List tags and show one in the preview window. Accepted and does nothing, as :ptag is.

pu[t].description: Put the text from register [x] linewise after [line] (default current line). Use line 0 to put above the first line.

py3.description: Run Python 3. Accepted and does nothing, as :python is.

py[thon].description: Run Python. Accepted and does nothing: there is no Python interface.

q[uit].description: Close the current editor. :close and :hide behave the same way as :quit in IdeaVim.

r[ead].description: Insert {file} below the cursor or line [range]; with :read !{cmd}, insert the output of {cmd} instead.

rec[over].description: Recover a file from a swap file. Accepted and does nothing: there are no swap files.

red[o].description: Redo one change that was undone.

redi[r].description: Send the messages that follow to a file, a register or a variable, until :redir END.

redr[aw].description: Redraw the screen. Accepted and does nothing: VS Code paints when it needs to.

redraws[tatus].description: Redraw the status line. Accepted and does nothing, as :redraw is.

reg[isters].description: Display the type and contents of all registers, or only of the registers named in {arg}.

res[ize].description: Set the window height to N rows or change it by +N or -N; without an argument, maximize it.

ret[ab].description: Replace the indentation in [range] to suit a new 'tabstop', given as [new_tabstop].

rew[ind].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

ri[ght].description: Right-align the lines in [range] within [width] columns, 'textwidth' by default.

rightb[elow].description: Make the following command put its new window below or right of the current one.

ru[ntime].description: Source {file} from the runtime path. Accepted and does nothing: there is no runtime path.

rub[y].description: Run Ruby. Accepted and does nothing: there is no Ruby interface.

rund[o].description: Read an undo file. Accepted and does nothing: undo is VS Code's and is not persisted.

rv[iminfo].description: Read a viminfo file. Accepted and does nothing: there is no viminfo file.

s[ubstitute].description: Substitute {pattern} with {string} in [range] lines, using [flags] (e.g. g for all matches, i to ignore case, c to confirm).

san[dbox].description: Run {cmd} in a sandbox, where it cannot change anything outside the text.

sav[eas].description: Write the buffer to {file} and edit that file from now on.

sb[uffer].description: Split the window and edit the buffer [N] in the new one.

sba[ll].description: Open a split window for each buffer in the argument list.

scr[iptnames].description: List the scripts that have been sourced, in the order they were.

scripte[ncoding].description: Specify the character encoding used in the script. Accepted for compatibility; it does nothing in IdeaVim.

se[t].description: Show or set options. Without arguments show all options that differ from their default value. See :set {option}, no{option}, {option}={value}.

setg[lobal].description: Like :set, but only show or set the global value of an option.

sethandler.description: Choose whether Vim or the IDE handles a shortcut, per mode, e.g. :sethandler <C-V> n-v:vim i:ide. Without a shortcut, apply to all conflicting shortcuts.

setl[ocal].description: Like :set, but only show or set the value of an option that is local to the current buffer or window.

sf[ind].description: Split the window and edit the file found along 'path'.

sh[ell].description: Open the IDE's Terminal tool window.

sign.description: Place, list and remove the markers Vim calls signs, in the gutter.

sil[ent].description: Run {cmd} without its messages. With [!] errors are silenced too.

sl[eep].description: Do nothing for [count] seconds, or {N}m milliseconds.

sm[agic].description: Like :substitute, with 'magic' on for the pattern whatever the option says.

smap.description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

smapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

smile.description: Display some ASCII art, chosen according to the type of the current file.

sn[ext].description: Split the window and edit the [count] next file in the argument list.

sno[magic].description: Like :substitute, with 'magic' off for the pattern whatever the option says.

snor[emap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

so[urce].description: Read and execute Ex commands from the file {file}.

sor[t].description: Sort lines in [range] (default: the selected lines, or the whole file). [!] reverses the order; flags: i ignore case, n numeric, u unique, r sort on /{pattern}/ match.

sp[lit].description: Split the current editor window in two, horizontally for :split and vertically for :vsplit. With [file], open it in the new split.

spe[llgood].description: Add {word} to the list of correctly spelled words.

spelld[ump].description: Dump the word list into a buffer. Accepted and does nothing: the spell checker is VS Code's.

spelli[nfo].description: Show which spell files are used. Accepted and does nothing, as :spelldump is.

spellr[epall].description: Repeat the last spelling correction everywhere. Accepted and does nothing.

spellra[re].description: Mark a word as rare. Accepted and does nothing, as :spelldump is.

spellw[rong].description: Add {word} to the list of misspelled words.

spr[evious].description: Split the window and edit the [count] previous file in the argument list.

st[op].description: Suspend the editor. Accepted and does nothing: there is no shell to return to.

sta[g].description: Split the window and jump to the tag in the new one.

star[tinsert].description: Start Insert mode, as with i. With [!], append at the end of the line, as with A.

startg[replace].description: Start Replace mode with the Visual selection, from where the cursor is.

startr[eplace].description: Start Replace mode, as with R. With [!], start at the end of the line.

stopi[nsert].description: Stop Insert or Replace mode and return to Normal mode.

sun[hide].description: Open a split window for each loaded buffer.

sunm[ap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

sus[pend].description: Suspend the editor. Accepted and does nothing, as :stop is.

sv[iew].description: Split the window and edit [file] read-only in the new one.

sy[ntax].description: Set the syntax of the buffer. VS Code decides the language; :set syntax={name} is the one that works.

t.description: Copy the lines in [range] to below line {address}.

tN[ext].description: Jump to the [count] previous matching tag.

ta[g].description: Jump [count] entries forward (newer) in the tag stack.

tab.description: Make the following command open a new tab instead of a new window.

tabN[ext].description: Go to the previous editor tab, wrapping around at the first one. With [count], go [count] tabs back.

tabc[lose].description: Close the current editor tab, or the tab given by {arg}: a tab number, +N or -N relative to the current tab, or the last tab.

tabe[dit].description: Open [file] in a new tab, or an empty buffer when no file is given.

tabf[ind].description: Find {file} along 'path' and open it in a new tab.

tabfir[st].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

tabl[ast].description: Go to the last file, buffer or tab.

tabm[ove].description: Move the current editor tab to after tab {N}, or +N/-N positions relative to its current place. Without {N}, move it to the end.

tabn[ext].description: Go to the next editor tab, wrapping around at the last one. With {N}, go to tab {N} (first tab is 1).

tabnew.description: Open [file] in a new tab, or an empty buffer when no file is given.

tabo[nly].description: Close all editor tabs except the current one.

tabp[revious].description: Go to the previous editor tab, wrapping around at the first one. With [count], go [count] tabs back.

tabr[ewind].description: Go to the first file, buffer or tab.

tabs.description: List the tabs and the windows in each, with the current one marked.

tags.description: Show the contents of the tag stack. The current entry is marked with >.

tc[l].description: Run Tcl. Accepted and does nothing: there is no Tcl interface.

tcd.description: Change the working directory for this window or tab only.

tch[dir].description: Change the working directory for this window or tab only.

tearo[ff].description: Tear a menu off. Accepted and does nothing: there are no Vim menus here.

tf[irst].description: Jump to tag [count] of the matches, the first by default.

tj[ump].description: Jump to the tag [name], listing the matches when there is more than one.

tl[ast].description: Jump to the last of the matching tags.

tm[enu].description: Set a menu tooltip. Accepted and does nothing, as the menu commands are.

tn[ext].description: Jump to the [count] next matching tag.

to[pleft].description: Make the following command put its new window at the very top or far left.

tp[revious].description: Jump to the [count] previous matching tag.

tr[ewind].description: Jump to tag [count] of the matches, the first by default.

trus[t].description: Mark a script as trusted. Accepted and does nothing: there is no trust database.

ts[elect].description: List the tags matching [name] and let one be chosen.

tu[nmenu].description: Remove a menu tooltip. Accepted and does nothing, as the menu commands are.

una[bbreviate].description: Remove abbreviation {lhs} for the mode of the command. Use <buffer> to remove a buffer-local abbreviation.

undoj[oin].description: Join the next change to the one before it, so one undo takes both back.

undol[ist].description: List the undo branches. Accepted and does nothing: undo is VS Code's.

unh[ide].description: Open a window for each loaded buffer.

uni[q].description: Remove the repeated lines in [range]. Flags: i ignore case, u only report, r match /{pattern}/.

unl[et].description: Delete the variables named. With [!] a variable that does not exist is not an error.

unlo[ckvar].description: Unlock the variable {name}, so it can be changed again. A [depth] also unlocks nested items.

unm[ap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

uns[ilent].description: Run {cmd} with its messages shown, inside a :silent.

up[date].description: Save the current file, but only if it has been modified.

v[global].description: Execute the Ex command [cmd] (default :p) on the lines in [range] (default whole file) that match {pattern}. With :g! or :v, use the lines that do not match.

ve[rsion].description: Show which Vimperor this is, and which editor it is running in.

verb[ose].description: Run {cmd} with 'verbose' set to [count], 1 by default.

vert[ical].description: Run :resize {cmd} on the window width instead of its height, e.g. :vertical resize +5.

vim[grep].description: Search for {pattern} in {file}... with Vim's own matcher and fill the quickfix list.

vimgrepa[dd].description: Like :vimgrep, adding to the quickfix list rather than replacing it.

viu[sage].description: Show Normal mode help. Accepted and does nothing: :help lists the commands instead.

vm[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

vmapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

vn[oremap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

vne[w].description: Split the window vertically and open a new, empty buffer in it.

vs[plit].description: Split the current editor window in two, horizontally for :split and vertically for :vsplit. With [file], open it in the new split.

vu[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

wN[ext].description: Save the current file and go to the [count]th previous editor tab.

w[rite].description: Save the current file. With {file}, write [range] lines (default all lines) to {file}; use [!] to overwrite an existing file.

win[size].description: Resize the editor window. Accepted and does nothing, as :winpos is.

winc[md].description: Run the window command {arg}, as if CTRL-W {arg} had been typed.

winp[os].description: Move the editor window. Accepted and does nothing: the window is VS Code's.

wn[ext].description: Save the current file and go to the [count]th next editor tab.

wp[revious].description: Save the current file and go to the [count]th previous editor tab.

wq.description: Save the current file and close its editor.

wu[ndo].description: Write an undo file. Accepted and does nothing, as :rundo is.

wv[iminfo].description: Write a viminfo file. Accepted and does nothing, as :rviminfo is.

x[it].description: Save the current file and close its editor.

xm[ap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

xmapc[lear].description: Remove all mappings for the modes of the command, e.g. :nmapclear for Normal mode. :mapclear! clears Insert and Command-line mode mappings.

xn[oremap].description: Map key sequence {lhs} to {rhs} in the modes of the command. The nore forms are not remapped. With only {lhs}, or nothing, list matching mappings.

xu[nmap].description: Remove the mapping of {lhs} for the modes of the command. :unmap! removes it from Insert and Command-line modes.

y[ank].description: Yank [range] lines (default current line) into register [x]. A [count] yanks that many lines starting with the last line in [range].

z.description: Print a window of text around the line in [range], the way :z does in ex.

~.description: Repeat the last :substitute in [range] lines. :& uses the same search pattern, :~ uses the last used search pattern. [&] keeps the flags.
